# domain-modeling

The schema is the last step, not the first. A field name chosen before the concept is agreed becomes
the concept — and then every reader inherits the confusion, because the shape now argues for itself.
This is a **lane requirement** in CONTROLLED (`harness/risk-policy.toml`), owed before `PLAN`: the
model has to exist before there is a plan to write against it.

## 1. Name the nouns

List the things the change is about, in the language the humans who own the domain actually use. One
name per concept, one concept per name. Two names for one thing is drift waiting to happen; one name
for two things is a defect that will be very hard to see later.

`docs/glossary.md` is the home of ubiquitous language here. It is **constitution plane** — read it,
align to it, and if your change genuinely introduces or contradicts a term, that is a proposal for a
human to ratify, not an edit you make. `gate-model` explains why that write is refused.

## 2. State each noun's invariant

For every noun: what must always be true of it? Not validation rules — invariants. "An interval's
end is never before its start." "A record's id is unique within its batch." "A null and an empty
string are different values."

An invariant you cannot state is a concept you do not yet have. An invariant nobody enforces is
prose; it belongs in a contract or a test, and `data-contracts` owns the contract mechanics.

## 3. Say where each noun is authoritative

Every value has exactly one place that decides it, and everywhere else holds a copy. Write down
which is which — the authority, and each derived copy with the rule that regenerates it.

This is what makes a later disagreement resolvable instead of a debate: `two-plane-memory` maps
which artifacts are human-owned truth and which are regenerated, and a copy that has drifted from
its authority is a bug in the copy by definition.

## 4. Draw the boundaries the nouns cross

For each noun that leaves its component: what carries it, and in what representation? In this repo
the language boundary is **process, file, or DB only** — never an in-process object — and the
canonicalization invariants for anything crossing it belong to `polyglot-boundary`. Do not restate
them; note which of your nouns cross, so the right rules get applied when the shape is written.

`pipeline-map` shows which stage produces and which consumes a given contract, so an edge with a
noun that does not line up end to end is visible before it is built.

## 5. Only now, the shape

Write the schema, the table, or the type — and check it says exactly what steps 1–4 said, with no
extra field that no invariant justifies and no missing field an invariant requires. A contract
change carries the drift and golden gates; `contract-check` is how you find out early.

Record the discipline in `<task_dir>/discipline/domain-modeling.json`, citing the model document in
`outputs`. `uv run python -m tools.discipline <task_dir>` reports what is still owed.
